_comment: Shared normalization fixture for the terminal font FAMILY (#866). Read by BOTH
tests/test_prefs.py and web/src/theme/termFont.test.ts so the Python and TypeScript
implementations cannot drift — and by web/e2e/terminal-font.spec.ts, which checks the
rows against a REAL CSS parser.
Three classes of rejection, each a defect that shipped in an earlier draft:
charset   — ';' '{}' '()' '<>' '\\' and newlines: the injection boundary.
structure — 'Menlo,,monospace', '"Fira Code', whitespace only: all-legal characters,
grammar   — '123, monospace', 'Font.Name', 'inherit': all-legal characters AND valid
structure, but the browser discards the whole declaration, so the stored
value and the live terminal disagree about which face is active.
The contract with the browser is ONE-directional: every write_accepted row must be
accepted by Chromium (asserted in the e2e), but not the converse — Chromium accepts
'"Fira Code' by auto-closing the string and accepts '--weird'; both are typos here.
browser_rejects holds the rows where BOTH must refuse, which is what pins the grammar.

GRAMMAR: a single leading hyphen is legal
GRAMMAR: digits are fine after the first character

GRAMMAR: digits are fine inside QUOTES

GRAMMAR: every classic generic behaves this way
